summary: Implement ZFS disk discovery, Core-owned provisioning and per-host local repositories, the Controller wizard and OpenZFS delivery recipe. API impact: new contract. Acceptance remains open as recorded in the QA report.

guide.reason: Operators select devices, confirm erasure and inspect per-host ZFS outcomes; existing-dataset registration remains available.

api.reason: New capability-gated zfs-device discovery and storage-zfs-provision operation, Core-owned per-host results and peer execution; Controller relays authenticated intent.

roadmap.reason: Record ZFS provisioning in development while master-change and external delivery acceptance remain open; completed native, kernel upgrade/recovery and offline image checks are recorded in QA.

state.reason: Pool repository identity, device selections, layout and outcomes remain recoverable independently of Controller.
state.record: The pool master keeps zfs-pool.json, zfs-lifecycle.json and its accepted command journal; each target Core keeps zfs-provision receipts and managed-vms registration records. Each native pool root filesystem carries nex:repository. A fresh Controller adopts master Inventory.managed storage and zfs_provisions, with per-host access; it does not derive or own repository identity.

verification.method: Executed checks and limitations are recorded in the rollout QA report; combined acceptance is still in progress, not inferred from test source or packaging configuration.
